title: Host-scheduled all-HiFloat8 GQA prefill
formula: out = softmax(Q @ K^T / sqrt(128)) @ V over one shared KV head, computed as score^T = K @ Q^T with P = 16*exp(s - rowmax) published in HiFloat8; HiFloat8 Q[M,128], K[N,128] and V[N,128] in uint8 carriers, BF16 out[M,128], FP32 state merged across host-owned key intervals
study_for: How to keep a probability inside a narrow float without paying for it per element: grep `LN16` in kernel.py. Biasing the running max by `-ln16` once makes `expsub` return `16 * exp(s - m)` for free, so the x16 threads through the row sum and the accumulator and cancels in the output, while the stored running max stays the true one. Compare `attention.a5_decode_fp8`, which spends a `muls` on every P element to get the same headroom.

The nz4 constant block records why each number is what it is, including the negatives: `FRAC_STRIDE4` is 33, not 32, because one pad row per NZ fractal dodges a bank conflict -- the same +1 shows up in every NZ P publication in this directory tree; `UNROLL4 = 2` says higher unroll gave no speedup; and `_DEINT_U8` is a flip-if-the-board-rejects-hif8 escape hatch that is off.

Both L0C drains, in production form: `DualMode.SPLITN` for the transposed score tile, because after `score^T = K @ Q^T` the query rows are its N axis, and `DualMode.SPLITM` for the PV result, where they are the M axis again -- grep both, the second is commented `each AIV its 64 query rows`. The rule is "split whichever axis carries the query rows", not "always SPLITM".

Only the HOST metadata generator is target-aware. The kernel reads `GetCubeNum()` and its own row of the per-core table, so the same body runs on a 32-core and a 28-core part as long as the generator emits that many rows -- see the comment block above `FA_NF`, and `reference.schedule`, which is that generator.
do_not_copy_when: You need the x16 to be visible in an intermediate you compare against a reference. It cancels only across the full numerator/denominator pair; a partial that escapes to the workspace still carries it.
Your buffer depth is not 3 or 4. `_CacheBuf = QBuff if CACHE >= 4 else TBuff` picks the buffer class from `CACHE`; another depth needs a different buffer type, not a different constant.
